chapter_name: Solar Radiation, Heat Balance and Temperature
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how the Earth gets its energy from the Sun, how it balances this heat so we don't burn up or freeze, and why temperature varies across the globe!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Insolation is the 'Incoming Solar Radiation'. The Earth intercepts only a tiny fraction of the Sun's energy. Because the Earth is round, the equator gets direct, intense sunlight, while the poles get slanted, weaker sunlight.

The Earth maintains a constant temperature by perfectly balancing heat. Whatever energy it receives from the Sun (shortwaves), it eventually sends back into space (longwave terrestrial radiation). If this budget breaks, the Earth would get progressively hotter or colder.

The sun doesn't heat the air directly. It heats the Earth's surface first. The surface then heats the air above it through Conduction (contact), Convection (upward movement of hot air), and Advection (horizontal wind).

Temperature isn't the same everywhere. It depends on Latitude (distance from equator), Altitude (height above sea level), and Distance from the Sea (oceans heat up and cool down much slower than land).

fun_activity.title: 🪞 The Albedo Effect Test
fun_activity.instructions: On a sunny day, place a piece of black paper and a piece of white paper on the ground. After 15 minutes, touch both. The black paper will be much hotter! White surfaces (like snow) have a high 'Albedo'—they reflect sunlight. Black surfaces absorb it.

exam_tips: 📌 'Albedo' is the proportion of solar radiation reflected back into space without heating the Earth. Earth's average albedo is about 35%.
📌 Terrestrial radiation (longwaves from the Earth) is what actually heats the atmosphere from below, which is why temperature decreases as you go higher up a mountain.
📌 Normal Lapse Rate: Temperature drops by 6.5°C for every 1000 meters you climb. 'Inversion of Temperature' is the rare opposite, where cold air is trapped below warm air.
quick_recap: ⭐ Insolation is shortwave radiation from the Sun; Terrestrial radiation is longwave from the Earth.
⭐ The heat budget ensures the Earth's average temperature remains relatively constant.
⭐ Water heats up and cools down much more slowly than land, causing coastal areas to have moderate climates.
